newsitem.title: UK: Latin America, East Europe seen attracting more FDI.
newsitem.headline: Latin America, East Europe seen attracting more FDI.

text.p: Latin America and Eastern Europe are attracting increasing flows of global foreign direct investment amid growing multinational investment in emerging markets, CrossBorder Capital managing director Michael Howell said.
Howell told a briefing organised by the American Chamber of Commerce that Latin America and Asia were beginning to change places as the most popular market for foreign direct investment.
He said a large chunk of international fixed and portfolio capital was going to emerging markets, providing a catalyst for growth in coming years.
"Emerging markets are playing catch-up, and this is being underwritten by Western pension funds and multinationals," he said.
A big slice of capital flows into emerging markets remained portfolio investment, he said, with nearly $60 billion in net portfolio equity investment into emerging markets expected in 1997.
He said emerging markets represented about 10 to 12 percent of portfolio investment, but were attracting some 25 percent of cash flows.
Howell said global FDI in emerging markets could hit $110 billion in 1997 against $95.6 billion in 1996, and much of this was being exported by developed countries.
The equivalent of one Ford Motor Co was being invested in emerging markets annually, he said.
The traditional market for global FDI was the Pacific Rim, but this was becoming saturated, with over-investment noticeable in some Asian markets.
But he said Latin America and Eastern Europe had turned around following initial concerns about investing there, with FDI in Africa and India expected to pick up in the next couple of years.
